transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m convinced I’ve figured out something so big in my work and art that normal rules and other people’s concerns just don’t apply to me right now. I’ve tapped into a vision that is completely revolutionary, and the usual limitations just don't make sense for what I'm trying to accomplish.

Have you ever had another period in the past when you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable for days, or a time when you felt very depressed for at least two weeks? Or is this the first time anything like this has happened?
I don't recall ever having any previous episodes like this in the past. This definitely feels like the very first time things have gotten this out of control for me.

During this time, have you also been feeling unusually high or irritable with much more energy and needing far less sleep than usual? Or did the strange beliefs come on without any major change in your mood or sleep?

The intense energy, barely sleeping, and these beliefs all started at the exact same time. I only get about three hours of sleep a night but wake up feeling totally wired and buzzing, though I do get really snappy if anyone questions my vision. I never had any of these thoughts about people tracking my work or trying to steal my ideas before this sleepless, supercharged phase began.

Have there been any times when the unusual beliefs or feeling that people were tracking or trying to steal your ideas continued even after your energy, mood, and sleep returned to normal? Or do those beliefs only happen during this high-energy, little-sleep period?

No, those beliefs only happen when I'm in this high-energy, sleep-deprived state. Before this intense phase started with the project, I never had any of those paranoid thoughts or felt like people were trying to steal my ideas. They are completely tied to this wired period.

final_diagnosis.reason: First lifetime episode characterized by markedly elevated/irritable mood, increased energy, decreased need for sleep, grandiose beliefs, and persecutory ideas occurring only during the mood episode. Psychotic symptoms are mood-congruent/tied to the manic state, supporting manic episode with psychotic symptoms rather than a primary psychotic disorder.
